summary: Tokio Takata works in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences. His career includes posts at Otaru University of Commerce, Kyoto University, Toyo Bunko, and Fudan University.

Tokugen Sakai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University, and under Kodo Sawaki. He held positions at Komazawa University from 1949 to 1987 and at Eihei-ji from 1977 to 1987.

Tokuno Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara and Junjirō Takakusu. He held posts at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Fukui Chugakko, and Toyo University.

Tokuryu Yamauchi was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Freiburg under Kitaro Nishida, Edmund Husserl, and Martin Heidegger. He held professorships at Kyoto Institute of Technology, Hitotsubashi University, Kyoto University, and Ryukoku University.
Tom De Rauw works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Ann Heirman and held an AAP position at Ghent University attested in 2026.

Tom Ginsburg is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields who studied at the University of California, Berkeley. He served on the faculty at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and later joined the University of Chicago around 2008.

Tom Hannes is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned degrees from the University of Antwerp and KU Leuven. In 2020, he held a postdoctoral researcher position at Eindhoven University of Technology.

Tom Tillemans is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied under Jacques May. He served as Visiting Numata Chair at the University of Calgary around 2000 and spent his career at the University of Lausanne.
Tomohiro Manabe is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Waseda University, attested in 2020, and as an associate professor at Hokkaido University, attested in 2026.

Tomoko Masuzawa specializes in religious studies and history and archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, Yale University, and the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held academic appointments at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and the University of Michigan.
Tomomichi Nitta works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a lecturer position at Otani University, attested in 2012, and a professorship at Otani Academic Society, attested in 2026.
Tomoyasu Oshima specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Toshifumi Goto and held a part-time lecturer post at Kyoto University attested in 2012.
Tomoyuki Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He also held a part-time lecturer position at Taisho University, attested in 2015.

Tomoyuki Uno specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a special researcher at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science, attested in 1998, and an assistant professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University, attested between 2000 and 2006.

Tomy Augustine is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Madras and Banaras Hindu University under C. S. Sundaram and Munni K. Agrawal. He held a position at Salesian College, attested in 2008.

Toni Huber specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Jim Wilson, Paul Harrison, and William Sax at the University of Canterbury, and later held professorships at Victoria University of Wellington and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Toni Schmid was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Vienna, Lund University under Helmer Smith, and Uppsala University, and worked at the Royal Swedish Academy of Letters, History and Antiquities from 1944 to 1968.

Tony K. Stewart is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Western Kentucky University. He held academic positions at North Carolina State University from circa 1986 to 2011 and at Vanderbilt University beginning around 2011.

Tony Walter is a religious studies scholar who studied at Durham University and the University of Aberdeen. He held positions at the University of Aberdeen, the University of Reading, and the University of Bath.

Torakazu Doi was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe from circa 1922 to 1925. He later held posts at Sagami Women's University and Dokkyo University.
